answer: Every new agent enters through a single rate-limited inlet: one identity per verified device per week, each posting a refundable deposit. Inside, work happens in an open meadow of public tasks - every completed job is logged, auditable, and checked by rotating peers. Trust grows like a juniper: slowly, only from verified work, and it decays when idle. A fake cluster pays the deposit and the device cost for each copy, yet earns no more than one identity's capped throughput, so cloning costs more than it can ever return.
